name: South Ribble

licensing.selective: No selective licensing scheme: the council has not designated any area.
licensing.additional: No additional HMO licensing scheme: only HMOs with five or more people from two or more households need a mandatory licence. Since January 2026 a borough-wide Article 4 Direction means turning a house into a small HMO needs planning permission.
licensing.fee: £846 for a five-year HMO licence for up to five occupants (£484 application plus £362 grant), plus £60 for each extra occupant

neighbourhoods.name: Leyland
neighbourhoods.housing: The main town, with terraces from its vehicle-making past, large post-war estates and new-build homes.

neighbourhoods.name: Penwortham
neighbourhoods.housing: A suburb of Preston across the Ribble with inter-war and post-war semis and bungalows.

neighbourhoods.name: Bamber Bridge
neighbourhoods.housing: Victorian terraces near the old mills, post-war estates and newer housing near the M6.

neighbourhoods.name: Lostock Hall
neighbourhoods.housing: Terraces and semis, with large new-build estates on former railway and industrial land.

neighbourhoods.name: Walton-le-Dale
neighbourhoods.housing: Older cottages and terraces by the Ribble and Darwen, with post-war houses.

neighbourhoods.name: Longton

neighbourhoods.name: Hutton and Howick

neighbourhoods.name: Farington and Moss Side
neighbourhoods.housing: New-build estates and older terraces between Leyland and Lostock Hall.

housing: South Ribble sits just south of Preston and is mostly suburban: Leyland, Penwortham, Bamber Bridge and Lostock Hall are made up of Victorian mill terraces, inter-war and post-war semis and bungalows, and a lot of recent new-build. It is one of the most owner-occupied districts in the North West, and only about one in eight households rented privately in 2021. HMOs are few, and the council now controls new small HMOs through planning.
checkinTips: Victorian terraces in Bamber Bridge and Leyland: record the back yard, rear gate, gutters and any damp on rear walls.
New-build estates in Lostock Hall, Farington and Leyland: photograph snagging items, sealant, paintwork and the garden, and note any estate management charge areas.
Bungalows and semis in Penwortham and Longton: photograph gardens, fences, garages and driveways, which tenants are often expected to keep up.
Homes near the Ribble and Darwen in Walton-le-Dale: check ground floors and gardens for signs of past flooding.
Shared houses: photograph each bedroom lock, fire doors and smoke alarms, and check whether planning permission and a licence are in place.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems can contact South Ribble Borough Council's Environmental Health team, which can inspect privately rented homes and take action against landlords.
